newsitem.title: SYRIA: Islamists vow fresh bombings against Israel.
newsitem.headline: Islamists vow fresh bombings against Israel.

text.p: Leaders of two Palestinian Islamic resistance groups and Lebanon's Hizbollah Shi'ite militia on Friday vowed fresh suicide bombings and military attacks against Israel.

"The era of booby-trapped cars will never end and will continue..the era of martyrs started a long time ago and it will continue for a long time...," Ammar Mosawi, politburo member of Lebanon's pro-Iranian Shi'ite Hizbollah militia said.
"I assure you that the martyrdom (suicide) operations are coming sooner or later," Ramadan Abdullah, leader of the Islamic Jihad group said.
A similar vow was also made by Mohammed Nazal, politburo member of the Islamic resistance movement Hamas.
The three were addressing a rally at the Yarmouk refugee camp near Damascus to commemorate the first anniversary of the killing of Yahya Ayyash, Hamas's master bomb-maker.
Ayyash, known as "the engineer" was killed in the Gaza Strip on January 5, 1996 by an exploding cellular telephone. Hamas blamed his assassination on Israel.
Moswai, Shallah and Nazal hailed Thursday's two bombings in Tel Aviv's central bus station that injured 13 people and said the attack was to "punish Israel for its crimes".
But none of the three claimed responsibility for the attack nor gave any hint as to which specific groups were responsible. Israel blamed Arab militias.
"The Tel Aviv bombing is a message to Israel that its crimes against Arabs would not go unpunished," the Hizbollah politburo member Mosawi said.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the bombings bore the hallmark of Palestinian "terrorist" attacks and vowed to respond with "extreme severity".
Hamas and Islamic Jihad are members of a 10-member radical Palestinian alliance that vowed to wreck a peace deal between Israel and the Palestinians.
Shallah backed Syria's accusation that Israel was involved in the bombing of a bus in central Damascus on New Year's eve that killed 11 and wounded 42.
"We got the message and we will respond in a language that that could not be understood except by the enemy," Shallah said.
Hamas and Islamic Jihad claimed several suicide bombings against Israel in which scores of people were killed.
Hizbollah, waging a war against Israeli presence in south Lebanon, also claimed several deadly attacks against Israeli forces.
"Hamas has not and will not change its policy. Resistance is our strategic option. Military operations will continue as long as the occupation is continuing," Mohammed Nazal said.
